problems: Owned list was empty (additions batch); the states chosen are the ones the scope names (Slovakia, Protectorate, occupation zones, Italian Social Republic) plus states other dossiers already use as counterpart slugs (saar-basin-territory, memel-territory) and the German occupation administrations of Poland, Ukraine and the Baltic.

memel-territory covers only 1920-1923 (League-protected stage); from January 1923 the land is Lithuanian and Cliopatria draws it in the Kingdom of Lithuania from 1924, so the autonomy of 1924-1939 is left to the kingdom-of-lithuania dossier.

nazi-germany dossier records the Italian Social Republic's land as occupation of kingdom-of-italy and has no vassal_start for italian-social-republic, slovak-republic is vassal there; the Protectorate, General Government and Reichskommissariats are recorded in their own dossiers as occupation_start/end with counterpart nazi-germany, the owner's side of the nazi-germany occupation events.

Cliopatria's Nazi Germany 1942 shape and the nazi-germany dossier already draw occupied Ukraine, the Baltic and Belarus; the reichskommissariat dossiers overlap them and the rendering step has to choose one.
Pages disagree on whether the German Operational Zones were part of the Italian Social Republic (RSI page footnote: still formally part; OZAK page: separate).
Reichskommissariat Ukraine page: oblast boundaries stand in for the Generalbezirke (the page names them without borders); the 340,000 km2 infobox area matches the 14 oblasts used (341,000 km2).
The Wikipedia page 'Hellenic State' is a name page only; the Greek puppet regime of 1941-1944 has no infobox article, so hellenic-state cites 'Axis occupation of Greece' and the Tsolakoglou page.

Disagreement between pages: Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia says 'Operation Uzice' began in late September 1941, the Republic of Uzice page says the First anti-Partisan offensive was in November 1941.
The italian-social-republic dossier shape leaves out the two Operational Zones (their own dossiers); the RSI page footnote says they were still formally RSI.
WebFetch extracts occasionally paraphrase; every quote in a note was checked against the extract's quoted text, but a few extracts were cut mid-sentence (Tsolakoglou appointment, Serbia dissolution).
